stem: Which of the following is the actual source of Son river?
expl: Two states– MP and Chhattisgarh have own claims and counterclaims regarding the origin of the Son River. The website of Anuppur district (M.P.) mentions that the origin of Son river is at a place called Sonmuda, located in Anuppur. In 1952-53, the then President Rajendra Prasad was shown the origin of the Son river at Sonmuda in Amarkantak (hill). Because of this reason, Sonmuda (Anuppur District, formerly part of Shahdol district) gained popularity and obtained public recognition as a place of origin of the Son river in various published sources. Chhattisgarh recognizes that the flow of Sonmuda from Anuppur joins the Arpa river via Amanala, Amadob Nala, and Mati Nala. Arpa joins the Mahanadi via Shivnath. According to Chhattisgarh, the actual origin of the Son river is Sonbachharwar village of Gaurela-Pendra-Marwahi district (formerly part of Bilaspur district) of Chhattisgarh. Factual details are available in support of Sonbachharwar in Authentic maps of the Sidhi District Gazetteer Survey of India (published during joint state of Madhya Pradesh and Chhattisgarh), the Archaeological Survey of India, 19th century A.D. and the book 'Son Ke Pani Ka Rang' by Dev Kumar Mishra. According to the India Water Resources Information Systems of the Ministry of Jal Shakti, Government of India, the source of Son River is located on the Amarkantak hill of Maikal mountain range in Chhattisgarh. According to the Envis Centre of the Ministry of Environment, too, the origin of Son River is in Pendra Road Tehsil. Presently this tehsil is located in Gaurela-Pendra Marwahi district of Chhattisgarh. See lines mentioned in the District Census Handbook Bilaspur published by the Office of the Registrar General and Census Commissioner, Government of India - According to saying, Son river originates from Amarkantak, but according to Geologists, this river originates from Sonekund, about 19 km. southeast of Pendra Road in Chhattisgarh. In fact, confusion originates also arises due to the fact that in both places, the origin of Son river is shown in the kund (pool). After this, the river flows underground. From the surface, the Son river flows from the village of 'Cholna' in Anuppur district. According to mythology, Son (male) and Narmada (female) are like lovers, and the origin of rivers of this type cannot be very close, i.e., from the same place. The rivers originating from the same place are in the form of brother and sister. Even if we view it from this perspective, the origin of Son seems to be inclined in favor of Chhattisgarh. What do aspirants do? • If the options as the source of Son are the Maikal mountain range or Amarkantak hill, then there is no problem as both the sites are situated on Amarkantak hill of Maikal mountain range. • If the option remains only Anuppur or only Sonbachharwar, then there is no problem as both places are recognized as the place of origin. • If both places are given in the options, first of all, it has to be seen in which state exam this question has been asked. If the question is asked in MP then answer must be Anuppur, and if the questions asked in Chhattisgarh, then the place of Chhattisgarh will have to be selected as the place of origin. • The language of the question also matters. For example there is the above question which is asked in U.P. P.C.S. but stated to be the 'original' place of origin. That is why the answer to this question has been considered as Son Bachharwar of Chhattisgarh. • It is also true that if the origin of the Son in Chhattisgarh is recognized, the number of states, districts and areas increases where Son river flows.

stem: Which one of the following Indian rivers forms an estuary?
expl: An estuary is a partly enclosed coastal body of water with one or more rivers or streams flowing into it, and with free access to the open sea. Estuaries form a transition zone between river environments and ocean environments and are subject to both marine influences, such as tides, waves, and the influx of saline water; and riverine influences, such as the flow of freshwater and sediments. The inflow of both seawater and freshwater provides high levels of nutrients in both the water column and sediment, making estuaries among the most productive natural habitats in the world. The St. Lawrence River makes the world's largest estuary, while the Narmada and Tapti (Tapi) make India's largest estuary.

stem: In the scheme of the physiographic division of India by S.P. Chatterjee in which sub-division of the Peninsular Plateau the Mahanadi Basin is included?

(5) The North Deccan. (6) The South Deccan. (7) The Western Ghats or Sahyadri (8) The Eastern Ghats. The Mahanadi Basin is included in the North Deccan Peninsula. The North Deccan (Maharashtra Plateau) : The plateau includes the entire state of Maharashtra, except the Konkan coast and the Sahyadri. The topography includes - the Mahanadi Basin, the Chhattisgarh Plains, Garjat Hills, and Dandakaranya.
